pairs.match: System for tracking changes to files over time, enabling comparison and reversion.
wrong_matches: Command to list files in a directory
The hidden folder where Git stores metadata
pairs.feedback_correct: Correct! Version control manages file history and versions.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That describes a shell command or .git directory, not version control.

pairs.match: Distributed open-source version control system that records snapshots of a project.
wrong_matches: Program for executing shell commands
Command that prints the working directory
pairs.feedback_correct: Git is the version control tool itself.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That describes the shell or pwd, not Git.

pairs.match: Program for typing and executing commands like git status.
wrong_matches: Distributed version control system
Command to change directory
pairs.feedback_correct: The shell is where you run Git and other commands.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That refers to Git itself or cd, not the shell.

pairs.match: Prints the current working directory path.
wrong_matches: Lists files and directories
Displays the Git version number
pairs.feedback_correct: pwd stands for 'print working directory'.
pairs.feedback_wrong: ls lists files; git --version shows the installed version.

pairs.match: Lists files and directories in the current location.
wrong_matches: Changes into a new directory
Initializes a Git repository
pairs.feedback_correct: ls shows the contents of a folder.
pairs.feedback_wrong: cd changes directory; git init creates a repository.

pairs.match: Changes the current directory to 'archive'.
wrong_matches: Prints the full path of the current directory
Displays the commit history
pairs.feedback_correct: cd moves the shell into a subdirectory.
pairs.feedback_wrong: pwd prints the path; git log shows history.

pairs.match: Displays the installed version of Git.
wrong_matches: Creates a new Git repository
Shows the current state of the working tree
pairs.feedback_correct: The double-dash flag shows Git's version.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git init creates a repo; git status shows file states.

pairs.match: A directory containing project files and a hidden .git metadata folder.
wrong_matches: Intermediate area for preparing changes
A recorded snapshot of the project
pairs.feedback_correct: A repo is the entire version-controlled project directory.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's the staging area or a commit, not a repository.

pairs.match: Hidden folder that stores all of Git's metadata and history.
wrong_matches: Command that initializes a new repository
A system to track changes in files
pairs.feedback_correct: .git contains the object database and configuration.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git init or version control, not the .git folder.

pairs.match: Creates a new directory and turns it into a Git repository.
wrong_matches: Checks the state of tracked and untracked files
Restores a file to a previous commit's version
pairs.feedback_correct: git init with a name creates and initializes a repo.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git status checks state; git checkout restores files.

pairs.match: Shows which files are tracked, modified, or staged.
wrong_matches: Displays the commit history
Compares two versions of a file
pairs.feedback_correct: status is the go-to command to see what's changed.
pairs.feedback_wrong: git log shows history; git diff compares changes.

pairs.match: When a .git directory exists inside another .git directory, causing confusion.
wrong_matches: A staging area that holds proposed changes
A unique identifier for a commit
pairs.feedback_correct: Nested repos make Git unsure which .git to use.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's the staging area or a commit hash, not nested repos.

pairs.match: Intermediate area where changes are placed before being committed.
wrong_matches: A compressed copy of a file's contents
A pointer to the current commit
pairs.feedback_correct: git add moves changes into the staging area.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's a blob or HEAD, not the staging area.

pairs.match: Stages all new and modified files in the current directory.
wrong_matches: Creates a new commit with a message
Restores a file from a previous commit
pairs.feedback_correct: The dot tells Git to stage everything beneath the current folder.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git commit or git checkout, not staging.

pairs.match: Creates a new snapshot with the message 'Fix typos'.
wrong_matches: Unstages a file from the index
Lists all commits since a date
pairs.feedback_correct: The -m flag supplies the commit message inline.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git restore --staged or git log --since.

pairs.match: A recorded snapshot of the repository including author, date, and message.
wrong_matches: The hidden directory that stores Git's objects
A command that shows what changed between commits
pairs.feedback_correct: Each commit represents a point in the project's history.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's .git or git diff, not a commit object.

pairs.match: A unique 40-character string that identifies a commit (deterministic).
wrong_matches: A Git object that stores file contents
A reference to the current branch tip
pairs.feedback_correct: The hash is computed from the commit's content.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's a blob or HEAD, not a commit hash.

pairs.match: Records the names and locations of files and directories in a commit.
wrong_matches: Stores the compressed content of a single file
A command to revert a commit without editing the message
pairs.feedback_correct: A tree maps file names to blobs and other trees.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's a blob or git revert --no-edit.

pairs.match: Short for binary large object; stores a file's content, not its name.
wrong_matches: A 40-character identifier for a commit
The intermediate area where changes are staged
pairs.feedback_correct: Blobs are content-addressable, so identical content is stored once.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's a commit hash or staging area.

pairs.match: Removes data.csv from the staging area, keeping working changes.
wrong_matches: Creates a new commit that undoes a previous one
Shows changes between two commits
pairs.feedback_correct: The --staged flag targets the index, not the working tree.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git revert or git diff.

pairs.match: Shows commit history in reverse chronological order.
wrong_matches: Displays details of a single commit
Compares the working directory to the last commit
pairs.feedback_correct: git log lists all past commits; press q to exit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git show or git diff.

pairs.match: Shows only the three most recent commits.
wrong_matches: Shows commits made after a certain date
Reverts the last three commits
pairs.feedback_correct: The -n flag limits the number of commits displayed.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's --since or git revert.

pairs.match: Displays commits made on or after April 2, 2024.
wrong_matches: Shows commits older than a given date
Compares two commits by date
pairs.feedback_correct: --since filters the log by a start date.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's --until or git diff with date refs.

pairs.match: Limits log output to commits before April 11, 2024.
wrong_matches: Shows commits from the last week
Deletes commits after that date
pairs.feedback_correct: --until defines the end of a date range.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's --since or git revert.

pairs.match: Displays metadata and diff for the commit with hash c27fa856.
wrong_matches: Lists all commits that touched a specific file
Stages a file for the next commit
pairs.feedback_correct: git show is for inspecting a single commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git log -- file or git add.

pairs.match: Shows unstaged changes between the working directory and the last commit.
wrong_matches: Shows changes between the staging area and HEAD
Creates a new commit that undoes a change
pairs.feedback_correct: Without --staged, git diff only compares unstaged modifications.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git diff --staged or git revert.

pairs.match: Compares what is staged to the last commit.
wrong_matches: Lists files that have been modified
Restores a file to a previous version
pairs.feedback_correct: --staged shows exactly what will go into the next commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git status or git checkout.

pairs.match: A symbolic pointer to the current commit (usually the tip of the current branch).
wrong_matches: The parent of the current commit
A command that limits log output
pairs.feedback_correct: HEAD moves when you check out a branch or commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's HEAD~1 or git log -n.

pairs.match: Refers to the commit two steps before the current one (grandparent).
wrong_matches: The current commit
A command to show the second commit in history
pairs.feedback_correct: Tilde notation walks back through the parent chain.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's HEAD or git show <commit>.

pairs.match: Creates a new commit that reverses the latest commit's changes, preserving history.
wrong_matches: Deletes the most recent commit
Compares two versions of a file
pairs.feedback_correct: Revert is a safe undo that does not rewrite history.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's reset (dangerous) or git diff.

pairs.match: Reverts the latest commit using the default message, skipping the editor.
wrong_matches: Reverts without creating a commit
Opens the editor to write a revert message
pairs.feedback_correct: --no-edit prevents the editor from opening.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's -n (no-commit) or the default behavior without --no-edit.

pairs.match: Applies the inverse changes but does not commit, leaving them staged.
wrong_matches: Commits the revert with a default message
Undoes the revert and keeps the original changes
pairs.feedback_correct: -n (--no-commit) stops before creating the commit.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's --no-edit or an incorrect interpretation.

pairs.match: Restores the file data.csv to its state from the previous commit.
wrong_matches: Stages data.csv for the next commit
Deletes data.csv from the working directory
pairs.feedback_correct: checkout with a commit reference and -- retrieves an old version.
pairs.feedback_wrong: That's git add or rm, not checkout.
